messages:
lee (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — noticed a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after last night's runtime deploy. p95 token latency up ~18% for some routes.
maya (perf): ugh. saw the alert. which model/route? any obvious change in kernel selection?
lee (eng-runtime): mostly on our long-context chat models (gpt-like-16k variants). profiler shows increased time in kv_lookup and attention kernel falling back to a generic path for several seq lengths.
tomas: stack traces? flamegraphs?
maya (perf): grabbed a sampling profile from the impacted instance. short dump:
```
# top functions by time
kv_cache::lookup 22.3%
attention::compute_generic 18.7%
kernels::fused_attention_vec fallback 12.1%
batching::assemble 9.8%
```
maya (perf): looks like kernel selection chose a non-fused attention for ~20% of requests (sequence lengths around 1024-1400). that increased kv_lookup churn.
olivia (infra): did the compile cache get invalidated during deploy? maybe new kernel binary shipped and JIT/compile warmed different code paths.
lee (eng-runtime): build manifest shows we bumped the attention microkernel to v2.1 which introduced a fallback for mixed quantization shapes. suspect the selector heuristic changed order.
sam (runtime): timeline: v2.1 rolled at 02:10 UTC with zero rollback. autoscaler triggered scale-up for a few clusters at 02:25. some deploy-time warmers kicked off.
nina (sre): ops-bot shows a scheduled prefill job hit the cluster at 02:15 with 500rps synthetic prefixes (we use the new prefill-generator). could that interact with autoscale-warmers?
ops-bot: scheduled-job "prefill-generator-job" started 2026-03-17T02:15:00Z for cluster:us-west-2-a, target-rps=500
maya (perf): possible chain: new kernel + warmers + autoscale = different batching distribution, causing the kernel selector to pick generic path and pollute KV cache with non-representative prefixes.
tomas: interesting — if warmers used synthetic prefixes that diverge from production prefix distribution, they can fill cache with low-value keys and push out hot keys. did we look at key cardinality during the prefill window?
lee (eng-runtime): yes, hit-rate by prefix shows a sharp drop during and after the job. prefill keys had ~3x higher entropy (more unique prefixes) than traffic baseline.
maya (perf): hypothesis: prefill load caused eviction of high-value KV entries and also changed batching heuristics (batches smaller/larger) which affected kernel selector heuristics. both reduced effective hit-rate and increased latency.
olivia (infra): immediate mitigation options: 1) pause scheduled prefill jobs 2) throttle prefill RPS 3) restrict prefill to non-production clusters 4) make prefill use representative prefix sampling.
sam (runtime): also can we make kernel selector prefer fused path for these seq lengths until we validate v2.1? i.e., override heuristic via runtime flag.
lee (eng-runtime): agreed — short-term: flip selector override on affected fleet + pause prefill job. medium-term: update prefill-generator to sample from real prefix distribution and add tenancy keying so warmers don't evict cross-tenant entries.
maya (perf): we should run a quick AB test: selector-override vs rollout baseline for a small fleet. measure p95, q95, cache hit-rate, and kernel selection counts.
tomas: experiment plan:
- 02:50 roll selector-override to 10% of us-west-2-a nodes
- enable detailed profiler for those nodes for 20 minutes
- compare metrics: prefix_hit_rate, kv_evictions, kernel_choice_distribution, p95_token_latency
- rollback after 30m if no improvement
lee (eng-runtime): I'll handle the rollout.
nina (sre): pausing prefill-job now. ops-bot?
ops-bot: scheduled-job "prefill-generator-job" paused by nina at 2026-03-17T02:38:12Z
olivia (infra): adding protection: future prefill jobs should be opt-in to cluster tag "can-prefill" and must declare prefix-sample: path/to/sample.json.
sam (runtime): added a runtime flag: --override-kernel-selector=fused_attention for seq-range 800-1600. ready to flip.
lee (eng-runtime): flipping to 10% now.
ops-bot: rollout started: config "override-kernel-selector" -> target 10% nodes in us-west-2-a at 2026-03-17T02:45:05Z
maya (perf): early numbers: prefix_hit_rate on experiment nodes +21% vs baseline. p95 token latency -14%. kv_evictions down ~30%. looks promising.
tomas: nice. we should also adjust warmers to use a "drip" pattern vs a burst — spread prefill across time windows and across AZs and ensure TTL-stable prefixes.
lee (eng-runtime): action items:
- lee: continue rollout to 30% if metrics hold (30m window)
- maya: generate a representative prefix sample from last 48h and hand to infra (deadline: +3h)
- olivia: enforce can-prefill tagging and sample requirement for scheduled jobs (today)
- sam: prepare a safer default for selector heuristics so next kernel bump won't regress (PR with tests) (EOD)
- tomas: add metric alerts for prefix_entropy spike and prefill_job_overlap with autoscale events (tomorrow morning)
nina (sre): will keep prefill paused for production clusters until we confirm safe config.
lee (eng-runtime): thanks all. quick note: when we re-enable warmers, prefer targeted warmers that honor tenant affinity and keep key cardinality low — e.g., prefill top-5k prefixes rather than random sampling.
maya (perf): one more long-term idea: autoscaler hook that signals "warm" state — don't run heavy prefill within X minutes of scale events to avoid odd batching interactions.
tomas: +1 to autoscaler cooldown hook. will prototype.
lee (eng-runtime): ok closing for now. will post a short doc w/ experiment results and new prefill runbook. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: thread archived by ops-bot at 2026-03-17T03:30:00Z
